title: Lesson 12 - Data Access Policies: OLS, FLS, RLS, and Dynamic Data Masking
description: Apply data governance requirements to platform configuration, focused on building object, field, and record level access policies and dynamic data masking with correct policy precedence.

questions.question: Two policies apply to the same field: one allows a group to read it, another denies the same group. What is the result?
options: Allow wins because it is more specific
Deny wins and access is blocked
The most recently created policy wins
questions.explanation: The rule of precedence is that a deny policy always overrides an allow policy, so access is blocked. The recency distractor is wrong because creation order does not matter; deny is always authoritative.

questions.question: A consultant needs service agents to see only the last four digits of a Social Security Number while finance sees the full value. Which governance feature fits?
questions.explanation: Dynamic data masking obscures sensitive values at query time and evaluates per user, so agents see redacted data while finance sees the full value. Object-level security is the strongest distractor and is wrong because it controls reach to the whole object, not partial visibility of one field.

questions.question: A team masks a field that another team uses as a join key in record-level security with joins. What happens?
options: The join query returns no results because the key values are masked
questions.explanation: Masking alters the key at query time, so the join finds no matches and record-level security with joins on masked keys returns nothing. The assumption that joins ignore masking is the strongest distractor and is wrong because joins evaluate the masked value.
